Subject: Commercial proposal & next steps for Horizon Analytics

Hi Kate / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday — useful to hear more about the MLOps bottlenecks and the Q4 pilot goal. As promised, I attached a short commercial proposal and an itemized estimate that aligns to the configuration we discussed (Reserved capacity with single-region VPC for initial pilot). Highlights: 

- Pilot scope: 3 endpoints, burst to 8 GPUs, estimated sustained throughput for 20 req/s
- Pricing: blended committed monthly rate + overage tier; estimate includes a 90-day pilot discount
- Timeline: onboarding + baseline tuning ~3 weeks, pilot evaluation 6 weeks

Attachments (stubs): Horizon-Proposal-Redwood-Estimate-v2.pdf (PDF, 42KB), Horizon-Commercial-Estimate-v2.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm receipt of the proposal
2) Quick 30-min walkthrough next week to align on assumptions and procurement questions
3) Marissa can run a technical spike if you want to validate latency on a representative prompt set

I have open windows on Wed 11/11 10:00–11:00 PT, Thu 11/12 15:00–16:00 PT, and Fri 11/13 09:30–10:30 PT. If those don't work, tell me a couple times that do and we’ll book.

Thanks,
Vivek

Apologies for the radio silence. We did receive the proposal and the spreadsheet — thanks, that was very clear. I was out at a customer site last week and procurement was tied up with a vendor RFP window.

A few quick notes from our side:
- The pilot timeline looks reasonable, but procurement wants to confirm data residency controls in the VPC option (specific questions around KMS integration and audit log retention).
- Budget owner asked if there is a one-time onboarding fee vs. spreading setup across the monthly committed rate. Can you confirm?
- We want a 30-minute walkthrough that includes someone from engineering — Tue 11/24 or Wed 11/25 morning PT would work for us.

Can Marissa join for the security/architecture portion? Also, can you re-send the XLSX version (our legal likes the line-by-line table)? I can circulate internally once we have the follow-up session recorded.
